svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Biomagnification: a persistent, fat-soluble pollutant becomes more concentrated at each trophic level. Example: DDT."], [1, "DDT in water at very low concentration is absorbed by plankton."], [3.5, "Small fish eat many plankton and store all their DDT."], [6, "Large fish eat many small fish."], [8.5, "Fish-eating birds at the top have the highest concentration: about ten million times that in the water."], [11, "DDT made eggshells thin, and bird-of-prey populations crashed until it was banned."]]
svg.title: Biomagnification
svg.desc: A food chain from water to plankton, small fish, large fish and fish-eating birds, with dots showing DDT becoming more concentrated at each level, and a logarithmic bar chart of typical DDT concentrations.
svg.text: Biomagnification of DDT in a food chain
Orange dots: DDT. Typical textbook values (parts per million, ppm).

g.data-info: DDT reaches lakes and rivers in run-off at very low concentration.
Absorb DDT and store it in their fat; they cannot break it down or excrete it (bioaccumulation).
Each fish eats very many plankton, so it collects the DDT from all of them.
Eat many small fish: the concentration rises again.
Top predators have the highest concentration. In birds of prey DDT caused thin eggshells that broke, so populations fell.
Each bar is about 10 to 25 times higher than the one below. Note the logarithmic scale.

g.text: about 8 million × the concentration in water
